identity_variants.criterion: Psychological causal continuity, with nonbranching or independently defended unique-branch rule
identity_variants.H_S_result: Conditional only. Causal quasi-memory/continuity must not presuppose the identity being proved; actual further experience beyond bodily death remains needed.
identity_variants.branching: Strict identity cannot identify two distinct successors with one predecessor. A unique-branch policy needs independent warrant, not convenience.
identity_variants.meaning_restoration: Continuity relevant to present projects can support concern and enhancement, but memory resemblance alone does not identify the same victim.

identity_variants.criterion: Persistence of the same human animal, with explicit biological cessation boundary
identity_variants.H_S_result: Under a cessation/no-resumption criterion, an irreversibly ceased organism cannot persist as the same animal. If a resurrection/restoration model is proposed, independently specify why the animal itself persists or returns; this corpus supplies no such observed case.
identity_variants.branching: A psychological copy is not enough to show persistence of the animal. Do not call conceptual disagreement about the boundary empirical survival.
identity_variants.meaning_restoration: Benefits to a successor or stored record are not automatically restoration of this animal-person.

identity_variants.criterion: Numerical identity of a simple subject or further-fact bearer
identity_variants.H_S_result: Conditionally permits continuity through memory loss and biological death, but must independently warrant the bearer, its determinate identity and actual experience beyond death. Stipulating a soul is not observing one.
identity_variants.branching: A further fact selecting one successor cannot be established merely because psychological evidence leaves two options.
identity_variants.meaning_restoration: Can preserve the same victim in a model, yet worthwhile and appropriately related continuation still requires more than bare sameness.

identity_variants.criterion: Strict numerical identity is the unchanged project target
identity_variants.H_S_result: All candidate criteria must satisfy same-person subjectivity beyond irreversible bodily death; interrupted consciousness alone neither proves nor disproves identity.
identity_variants.branching: Two distinct successors cannot both be strictly identical to one original.
identity_variants.meaning_restoration: Bare numerical survival may fail present-aim relatedness or worthwhile continuation.

identity_variants.criterion: Prudential psychological continuity or successor concern
identity_variants.H_S_result: Renamed target X-T17-SUCCESSOR-CONCERN; it does not satisfy unchanged H-S merely by being valuable or allowing branching.
identity_variants.branching: Concern can extend to multiple successors without making them one numerically identical person.
identity_variants.meaning_restoration: May preserve projects and benefit successors; this differs from original-victim restoration and requires its own value judgment.

history_models.H_S: Possible if actual future subjectivity crosses the death boundary under an adequate same-person criterion; not evidenced just by model construction.
history_models.H_T: Not required for the person or foundation.
history_models.H_P: Narrow subjectivity preservation follows if H-S obtains.
history_models.meaning: Worthwhile continuation can enhance significance; duration alone does not ensure worth.

history_models.model: M2 timeless foundation with temporal persons
history_models.H_S: Requires actual personal continuation in addition to a timeless foundation; one does not entail the other.
history_models.H_T: Foundation specified as non-successive; persons may have sequential experience without contradiction in the same bearer/respect.
history_models.H_P: Could preserve records or subjects; target must be specified.
history_models.meaning: Enduring benefit requires same-person temporal goods, not merely the foundation knowing finite lives.

history_models.H_S: Fails to supply the required additional subjectivity beyond the bodily-life boundary.
history_models.H_T: Timeless inclusion does not extend the included subject-history.
history_models.H_P: Can conditionally preserve a finite history or representation.
history_models.meaning: Preserved significance of a finite life is not extra lived continuation.

history_models.H_S: Can satisfy target if the enlarged history actually includes same-person subjectivity beyond death; that is a substantive assumption, not independent evidence.
history_models.H_T: Non-successive foundation can conditionally include an ordered enlarged history.
history_models.H_P: Narrow subjectivity preservation follows if enlarged same-person history is actual.
history_models.meaning: Possible enhancement and victim restoration require worthwhile, appropriately related further experience.

history_models.H_S: Does not satisfy same-person subjectivity target.
history_models.H_T: No entailment; record bearer may be temporal or stipulated timeless.
history_models.H_P: Can satisfy only specified record/value preservation, with actual bearer and persistence still needing warrant.
history_models.meaning: Records or successors may matter, but compensation to others is not automatically original-victim restoration.
